title: Dairy-Free Coconut Dream Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft coconut milk cupcakes topped with whipped coconut frosting, ready in 43 minutes with 25 minutes of prep.
description: These cupcakes use full-fat coconut milk in the batter, so they stay moist without any dairy. The crumb is soft and slightly dense, like a good coconut cake should be. On top goes a whipped coconut cream frosting. It is light, not too sweet, and holds its swirl if you chill the coconut cream first. I tested this recipe in my home kitchen with three coconut milk brands before landing on the ratio that works best. Toasted coconut flakes on top add crunch and make these look bakery style. This is a good pick for anyone avoiding dairy but still craving a rich, tropical cupcake.
ingredients: 1/2 cup full-fat coconut milk (canned, well shaken)
1/2 cup coconut oil, melted and cooled
2 cans (13.5 oz each) full-fat coconut milk, chilled overnight
1/2 cup toasted coconut flakes, for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, mix the 1/2 cup coconut milk, melted coconut oil, eggs, and vanilla until smooth.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir just until combined, then fold in shredded coconut.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
While cupcakes cool, open the chilled coconut milk cans. Scoop only the solid cream on top into a cold mixing bowl, leaving the liquid behind.
Beat the coconut cream with powdered sugar for 2 to 3 minutes, until light and fluffy with soft peaks.
Pipe or spread the whipped coconut cream onto fully cooled cupcakes.
Sprinkle toasted coconut flakes on top and serve, or chill until ready to eat.
tips: Chill your coconut milk cans for at least 8 hours, or overnight, so the cream firms up enough to whip.
Do not shake the chilled cans before opening. Shaking mixes the cream back into the liquid.
Toast the coconut flakes in a dry skillet over low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring often so they do not burn.
If your kitchen is warm, keep frosted cupcakes in the fridge until you are ready to serve them.

faq.question: Can I use coconut milk from a carton instead of canned?
faq.answer: No, carton coconut milk is too thin for this batter and will not whip for the frosting. Use canned full-fat coconut milk for both parts.

faq.question: Why did my coconut whip frosting turn out runny?
faq.answer: This usually means the coconut milk was not chilled long enough, or some liquid got scooped in with the cream. Chill the cans overnight and scoop carefully.

faq.question: How long do these cupcakes stay fresh?
faq.answer: Store frosted cupcakes in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 3 days. The coconut cream frosting softens at room temperature, so keep them chilled.

faq.question: Can I make the cupcakes ahead and frost them later?
faq.answer: Yes, bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Whip the frosting fresh right before serving.

conclusion: These coconut dream cupcakes prove dairy-free baking can still taste rich. The coconut milk batter and whipped coconut frosting work together for a soft, tropical bite. Give them a try next time you need a dairy-free treat for a crowd.
